## Structure and phase transitions in perovskites {#structure}

Perovskite oxides, simple ABO₃ and double A₂BB′O₆, distort from their ideal cubic structure through octahedral tilts, cation ordering and off-centre displacements, and those distortions decide their magnetic, dielectric and transport properties. For thirty years I have determined the crystal structures of these materials and followed their phase transitions with temperature, using laboratory and synchrotron X-ray powder diffraction, neutron diffraction and Raman spectroscopy. Eighteen experiments at the Institut Laue-Langevin, the ESRF and the SINQ source at PSI, fifty-three days of beam time in total, belong to this line, together with four of the five doctoral theses I have directed.

The method that ties the work together is symmetry-mode analysis, or mode crystallography: describing a distorted structure not by atomic coordinates but by the amplitudes of the symmetry-adapted modes of the parent phase, as implemented in the Bilbao Crystallographic Server's AMPLIMODES. My own contribution, developed on K₀.₅Na₀.₅NbO₃ and the Sr₂MM′O₆ families with M′ = Sb, W, Mo, Ru, Te, is a parametrised refinement protocol: high-resolution data on one member of a family fix the relations among mode amplitudes, and those relations let laboratory X-ray data, which cannot resolve light elements or subtle tilts on their own, be refined to a physically meaningful solution. It reduces the need for expensive high-resolution experiments and makes preliminary data usable.

## Thermal radiative properties of materials {#radiation}

Since 2018 I work in Thermomat, the research group on the thermophysical properties of materials at UPV/EHU, which operates HAIRL, a high-accuracy infrared radiometer built in-house: directional spectral emissivity from 0.83 to 25 μm, from room temperature to 1000 °C, in controlled atmosphere, with a full uncertainty budget. I am one of the group's two principal investigators. My part of the work is on the instrument and its data rather than on the samples: the model-free cascaded temperature control of the emissometer, the updated measurement method and uncertainty budget published in *Metrologia*, the "fer" framework for FAIR-compliant reporting of traceable experimental results, and EKHI, the open database of optical and thermal radiative properties of solids described in *Scientific Data* and indexed as a reference resource by emissivity.org. The materials side of the line ranges from oxidising steels and nuclear alloys to laser-patterned surfaces and emissivity-engineered coatings for concentrated solar power.

## Computation in physics education {#teaching}

The third line began as a way of teaching thermodynamics and became research. Jupyter notebooks written in Basque are the laboratory notebook of a theory course: the students derive, compute and plot in the same document, and the course keeps a daily log of what was done. MinervaLab, an interactive simulation laboratory for first-order phase transitions and the van der Waals fluid, was built as a bachelor's thesis under my direction, released under the GPL, and is the basis of the physics-education contributions I have presented at CSEDU 2017, GIREP 2018 and the Spanish Physical Society's biennial meeting in 2019, and of the teaching-innovation project on the electronic laboratory notebook that I led at UPV/EHU. The same tools now serve a different question: what the data say about how students perform, from the course's own records to the physics entrance examination across the Spanish regions.

## Projects and facilities

Ten recognised research groups and twenty-one competitive projects as of 2020, among them the Basque Government's ELKARTEK programme (2018–2019, co-principal investigator for the UPV/EHU node), the Spanish national plan (MAT2012-34740; MINECOG15/P65, 2016–2018), and infrastructure grants for a high-temperature infrared camera. Eighteen experiments at European large-scale facilities, worth about 550 000 € of beam time, several as principal investigator.
